findings.issue: The pairing's CPU cost is unbounded and falls outside the one deadline. It runs after all the runs, and nothing checks the clock during it. For every ambiguous failing line, _forced_label rebuilds the label sets and runs one Kuhn matching per candidate right. Each place() call re-sorts its candidates, and identical labels drive the augmenting path as deep as the line count. The loop repeats this for every failing line, including ones with an identical label. Measured with the functions (probe14): N identical ambiguous labels take 0.07 s at 20, 1.53 s at 40 and 47 s at 80, about N^5. Distinct labels grow quadratically: 3000 take 18.9 s. Real tool with --timeout 5 (probe15 and probe16), where a loop prints one label per item and the task edits the loop's assertion: 60 items took 10.6 s and 100 items took 136 s. Extrapolated, about 130 items pass HOST_BASH_LIMIT (600 s). The host then kills the helper before its finally, so the throwaway is stranded. The recursion depth also equals the chain length, so at about 1000 the result is a RecursionError. That surfaces as an uncaught traceback, exit 1, which is E_NOT_RED's code ('the test PASSED').

P82.8 says a red HEAD run is credited only on a count showing it covered every case, and names 'a house tally whose total equals the cases named' as that count. But the house harness keeps no list of cases. Its total is the number of check() calls that actually ran, and each of those prints exactly one PASS/FAIL line, so total == len(names) holds for every house run by construction. The only house runs this refuses are ones that print an escape line (a body or stage raise, or DUPLICATE CASE ID): those count in the total but are left out of the names. That is why probe17's e-body and e-stage are refused, and it is incidental. A suite that stops quietly (a `return` after a red) prints a tally that matches exactly. That case is already in HEAD's file and never passes (mine.v == 99). HEAD's run tail is ['FAIL the value is two (saw 1)', '', 'SELFTEST FAILED: 0/1 cases passed']. summary:
red-first names the task's own failing case, and proves it only against a green, isolated baseline of HEAD's tests.

What red-first now does:
- A house case whose label starts with an ordinary word is recognised.
- An expected unittest ERROR: line is not read as a failing case.
- HEAD's baseline always runs first, in an isolated throwaway: a fresh home, its own TMPDIR, and a forced checkout and clean. The task's new test files are laid over it as empty stubs, and the baseline must be green on one runner's tally.
- The task's tests must be red on HEAD's code, and the fix run must pass every failed case.

A failure is credited only when all of these hold:
- the runner locates it in one declared test file;
- the class the runner names defines it by its last binding;
- no HEAD test file anywhere holds an identical definition under the same class chain.

A later attribute assignment or literal setattr that replaces the case means the file does not define it. A house suite identical to a HEAD test module is refused.

The documents name the limits that remain: cosmetic edits, helpers, a house suite's missing locations, Python before 3.11, bindings nested in compound blocks, decorators, and computed setattr names.

R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:374-423 (_closest_literals, _standing): This is a regression introduced by P82.2, and it gives a false proved. The score for 'most specific' is the total fixed text of any literal that renders ANY form of the label, and that includes the full FAIL line with its detail. Suppose the working tree adds a literal that spells the printed line, such as a test asserting on the harness's output: EXPECT = 'the next value is read (saw %r)'. That literal then outranks HEAD's exact literal 'the next value is read'. The closest literal is not in HEAD, so an EXISTING case whose condition was edited to go red counts as the task's own. P82.1 refused this case, because HEAD's exact literal rendered the label. No sr case covers this shape. -> Rank a placeholder-free literal equal to a form of the label above any template. Among exact renderings, take the longest form. Fall back to the most specific template only when no literal renders the label exactly. That way the detail never outranks the label, and a new parenthetical label ('the value (as read)') still beats an unrelated exact 'the value'. The rule for all of them: a false proved must be impossible, so any case the two runs cannot be matched one to one is a refusal, never a credit. (F1) refuse when any case HEAD's run named is printed by the task's run in no label form (a label carrying a per-run value no longer lines up), and when a label is printed more often by the task's run than by HEAD's while one of those prints is a failure (F4: an edited case plus a new passing case of the same label). (F2) refuse when HEAD's run collected no case while a declared test file exists at HEAD, and when HEAD's run is red and may have stopped early (pytest 'stopping after' / 'Interrupted:', or a stop-first flag in the command: -x, --exitfirst, --maxfail, --sw, --stepwise, -f, --failfast). (F3) a declared test path that exists at HEAD but is absent from the working tree - a rename or a delete - makes the case set not comparable: refuse, and remove a deleted declared file from the throwaway so HEAD's put-back is exact. (F5) unittest names are qualified by class. (F6) HEAD's copies are restored byte for byte (git checkout HEAD -- <files>, or raw bytes). (F7) every git call of the put-back and the new-file check runs under the one deadline. (F8) _held_by_head's docstring and the guide name every limit that remains, all of them in the could-not-prove direction; the commit claim that said so falsely is corrected in this task's record. Each shape from probe12/probe13 as a red case, with the allow cases sr50, sr67, sr74, sr88, sr93, sr94 still proving.

tasks.title: red-first proves only against a green, isolated baseline, and every failure then is the task's own
tasks.description: Seven review rounds each found another way to credit a case past a RED baseline (probe20 (A), (C) this round). Every one of them depends on crediting while HEAD's own run is red, so the rule changes instead of growing another reader. New rule, one mechanism: (1) the task's tests run against HEAD's code and must be red with an assertion failure (as now). (2) HEAD's own test files run against HEAD's code in an ISOLATED checkout - a clean throwaway (checkout -f of HEAD plus clean -ffdx, so nothing the task's run wrote survives), PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, its own TMPDIR - and must be GREEN: a tally, no failure, no error. Anything else is could-not-prove with the reason "the command is already red (or unreadable) at HEAD - narrow it to the task's cases". (3) the task's tests run against the working tree's code (the fix run) and every case that failed in (1) must pass there; otherwise could-not-prove. (4) with (2) green, every failure in (1) comes from the task's change to the tests, so all of (1)'s failures are the task's own; --case must name one of them. Remove what this makes unnecessary - label matching and pairing (compare_runs, changed_reds, _uncovered, _hopcroft_karp and its SCC pass, the stop-first readers) - keeping one mechanism. Rewrite or remove the cases of removed functions with a reason each; every probe (probe5-probe21) must answer correctly, and a red baseline must now read could-not-prove with the narrowing reason. The docs, audit-executor.md and execute-task.md state the new rule and the narrowing instruction.

tasks.title: red-first always runs the baseline with the task's new test files as empty stubs, and credits only a failure located in a declared test file
tasks.description: Round-9 review (review-P82i.json; probe23, probe24). (1) baseline_skip read argv and was evaded by a second argument, a wrapper, a node id, a glob, a working-tree/HEAD mismatch. HEAD's baseline is ALWAYS made, in its isolated throwaway, with every declared test file that is new at HEAD laid over as an EMPTY file and nothing else of the task's, so the same command reaches exactly what the task's run reaches minus the task's cases, however it is spelled. (4) sr134 and sr135 pin E_NOT_RED and the note; sr140's replacement rows cover a dotted name, a node id into an old file and an sh -c script. (5) No further isolated run is made once less than a second of the deadline is left; the budget comment describes the code. Each probe23/probe24 shape (E1, E2, E2s, E3, E6, node id) a red case proved first; an allow case in sr138's shape (a command naming only a new test file) still proves, now with a stub baseline.
